summary: DEF-013. Adds public.profiles.email_signature (nullable text) and repoints /settings/my-profile at it. The page previously read and wrote organization_users.email_signature, a column that does not exist, so every load returned SQLSTATE 42703 and every save silently failed. One additive nullable column; no existing column, constraint, policy or trigger is altered.

problem.symptom: A staff member could type a signature, be told it saved, and have nothing stored. Engagement letters and system emails then went out unsigned with no indication why — another instance of the Gate 6 pattern the audit called out as the product's largest risk.
problem.root_cause: The UI targeted organization_users.email_signature. That column has never existed; PostgreSQL returned 42703 on both the read and the write.
problem.ruling: Owner, 2026-07-28: the signature lives on profiles.email_signature. The staff member owns their personal signature; practice branding and the legal footer remain organisation-level settings.
problem.why_profiles_is_right: It also makes it true by construction that one person has ONE signature, rather than a different signature per practice membership — which is what an organization_users column implies, and which contradicts the launch ruling that one identity belongs to one practice.
problem.no_backfill: There is nothing to migrate. The column the app wrote to never existed, so no prior value exists anywhere.

expected_objects.object: column public.profiles.email_signature text, nullable, no default
expected_objects.verify_via: db_schema -> public.profiles.email_signature type text, is_nullable = YES, no column default. Confirm no other column on profiles changed.

Set a signature, save, reload the page and confirm it persists; then db_select profiles for that user id and confirm the stored value matches. Before this release the same actions reported success and stored nothing.

expected_objects.object: A staff member with no signature can still send an engagement letter and system email
expected_objects.verify_via: With email_signature NULL, send an engagement letter and confirm it queues and renders normally. NULL means 'no personal signature', never a failure — this is the regression that would matter.

rollback.assessment: Forward-only but trivially reversible: DROP COLUMN would discard any signature staff have since saved. Reverting the app change alone restores the broken behaviour.
rollback.data_risk: None on apply. One additive nullable column; no data is read or written by the migration.

steps: Apply 20260728150000_profiles_email_signature.sql via the Lovable migration flow.
Confirm the card returns green AND a row exists in supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (verify against LIVE, not just Test).

Confirm profiles' existing RLS lets a staff member read and update their OWN row — the page writes under the user's session, so an over-restrictive policy would leave the save failing for a different reason.
After apply: refresh docs/audits/unapplied-migrations-baseline.json with the new applied version.
Notify Claude to run the expected-object verification and complete this receipt (move out of pending/).

post_apply_followups: Nothing yet CONSUMES profiles.email_signature. The audit's observed impact — engagement letters and system emails sent without the staff signature — is only half-closed by storing it: send-engagement-letter and the email templates must render it, treating NULL as empty. That is the next increment and is what actually closes DEF-013.
Confirm profiles has an RLS policy allowing a user to UPDATE their own row. If it does not, the page will still fail to save — with a different error code, which would look like this fix not working.
